saved_record.correction_summary: Removed the unnecessary INR 4.8 and 'within the hour' precision because neither is needed to establish the tested indication. Reframed the scenario using the exact labeled indications of acute major bleeding and urgent surgery. Rebuilt all distractors so they can be adjudicated directly from KCENTRA §§1 and 2.1 without relying on secondary claims about protamine, platelets, or oral vitamin K onset. Added a specific Educational Objective and adjusted difficulty from hard to moderate.
saved_record.educational_objective: For an adult receiving warfarin who requires urgent reversal because of acute major bleeding or urgent surgery, anticipate KCENTRA administration with concurrent vitamin K.
saved_record.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Administer vitamin K alone now and wait for a repeat INR before giving any coagulation-factor replacement.","B":"Administer KCENTRA alone now because concurrent vitamin K is unnecessary once coagulation factors are replaced.","C":"Delay KCENTRA until after surgery because it is indicated for major bleeding but not urgent procedures.","D":"Administer KCENTRA now with concurrent vitamin K to provide urgent reversal of warfarin anticoagulation."}}
saved_record.rationale: KCENTRA is indicated for urgent reversal of vitamin K antagonist therapy in adults with acute major bleeding or a need for urgent surgery or an invasive procedure. Its prescribing information also directs concurrent administration of vitamin K. Therefore D is the best answer. A omits the indicated coagulation-factor replacement strategy for this urgent-reversal scenario. B incorrectly omits concurrent vitamin K. C directly conflicts with the labeled indication for urgent surgery or invasive procedures.
